Spatial poolers for convolutional activations

Source: R/hierarchy_poolers.R
poolers.Rd

A pooler turns a 4-D activation tensor (N images x H x W x C channels) into an N x P feature matrix. The constructors below only describe how to pool; pool_activations does the work, and vgg_hierarchy_spec assigns one pooler to each network stage.

Usage

global_average_pool()

global_max_pool()

identity_pool()

Value

An object of class imfeatures_pooler: a list holding the pooler type and its parameters.

Details

ConstructorColumns per channelWhat is kept
global_average_pool()1Mean over all positions
global_max_pool()1Maximum over all positions
adaptive_grid_pool(ny, nx)ny * nxMean in each cell of a coarse grid
dct_pool(ny, nx)ny * nxMean plus low spatial frequencies
radial_pool(breaks)length(breaks) - 1Mean in each centre-to-periphery ring
identity_pool()H * WEvery position (flattened)

Every pooler writes its columns channel by channel: all spatial features of channel 1, then all of channel 2, and so on. pooler_feature_names returns the matching column names.

Dense activations (N x P matrices, such as fc1 or logits) have no spatial axes. Every pooler returns them unchanged.

Functions

  • global_average_pool(): Mean over height and width; one column per channel.

  • global_max_pool(): Maximum over height and width; one column per channel.

  • identity_pool(): No pooling. Dense matrices pass through unchanged; 4-D maps are flattened to H * W * C columns ordered by channel, then width, then height (height varies fastest).

Choosing a pooler

  • Use global_average_pool() when you want one number per channel and do not care where in the image a feature occurred.

  • Use global_max_pool() for the same size when presence of a feature matters more than its extent.

  • Use adaptive_grid_pool() to keep coarse location in non-negative, directly interpretable cells.

  • Use dct_pool() to keep coarse layout as a mean plus smooth spatial contrasts. The first column per channel equals global average pooling, so the remaining columns add layout to the usual summary.

  • Use radial_pool() when eccentricity (centre versus periphery) is the spatial variable of interest.

  • Use identity_pool() for dense layers, or for small maps where you want every position.

See also

pool_activations, pooler_feature_names, vgg_hierarchy_spec, and vignette("spatial-pooling", package = "imfeatures").

Examples

# Two images, an 8 x 8 map, three channels (N x H x W x C)
a <- array(rnorm(2 * 8 * 8 * 3), dim = c(2, 8, 8, 3))

dim(pool_activations(global_average_pool(), a))    # 2 x 3
#> [1] 2 3
dim(pool_activations(adaptive_grid_pool(2, 2), a)) # 2 x 12
#> [1]  2 12
dim(pool_activations(dct_pool(3, 3), a))           # 2 x 27
#> [1]  2 27
dim(pool_activations(radial_pool(), a))            # 2 x 9
#> [1] 2 9
dim(pool_activations(identity_pool(), a))          # 2 x 192
#> [1]   2 192

# The first DCT column of each channel is the global average
all.equal(
  pool_activations(dct_pool(3, 3), a)[, 1],
  pool_activations(global_average_pool(), a)[, 1]
)
#> [1] TRUE
